name: idyll-explorer-v2:reference
source:
[data name:"sales" source:"sales-data.json" /]
[var name:"category" value:"All" /]
[var name:"minimum" value:0 /]
[derived name:"rows" value:`sales.filter(row => (category === "All" || row.category === category) && row.sales >= minimum)` /]
[derived name:"total" value:`rows.reduce((sum, row) => sum + row.sales, 0)` /]
[derived name:"average" value:`rows.length ? total / rows.length : "—"` /]
# Exploring Sales Across Categories

Monthly sales can vary considerably across product categories. A useful comparison starts by choosing which records to examine.

## Choose Your View

Select a product category and a minimum sales value. A record should appear only when it matches both selections.

[Select value:category options:`["All", "Books", "Games", "Music"]` /]
[Range value:minimum min:0 max:500 step:10 /]

## Inspect the Records

The table shows the records included in the current selection. The chart presents those same records over time, making individual observations easier to compare.

[Table data:rows /]
[Chart data:rows type:"point" x:"month" y:"sales" color:"category" /]

## Summarize the Selection

The number of matching records, total sales, and average sales describe the current selection. These summaries should change whenever either control changes.

Matching records: [Display role:"count" value:`rows.length` format:".0f" /]
Total sales: [Display role:"total" value:total format:".2f" /]
Average sales: [Display role:"average" value:average format:".2f" /]

## When Nothing Matches

Some combinations of category and minimum sales may produce no matching records. In that case, the article should clearly explain that there are no results.

[Conditional if:`rows.length === 0`]No matching records.[/Conditional]

tests.label: Table and chart apply both filters for every control combination
Reactive record count, total, and average
Empty results clear both views and show the required message

name: idyll-story-v2:reference
source:
[data name:"sales" source:"sales-data.json" /]
[var name:"category" value:"Books" /]
[var name:"threshold" value:150 /]
[var name:"stage" value:0 /]
[derived name:"selected" value:`sales.filter(row => row.category === category)` /]
[derived name:"chartRows" value:`stage < 2 ? sales : selected` /]
[derived name:"reference" value:`stage === 2 ? sales.filter(row => row.category === "Books").map(row => ({month:row.month, sales:sales.filter(item => item.month === row.month).reduce((sum,item) => sum + item.sales,0) / sales.filter(item => item.month === row.month).length})) : []` /]
[derived name:"highlighted" value:`stage === 3 ? selected.filter(row => row.sales > threshold) : []` /]
[derived name:"focus" value:`stage === 1 ? category : ""` /]
[derived name:"stageName" value:`["Overview", "Focus", "Average", "Threshold"][stage]` /]
# A Closer Look at Monthly Sales

A single chart can answer different questions depending on what we choose to emphasize. Scroll through this article to examine the same sales data from four perspectives.

[Scroller step:stage]
[Step index:0]
## 1. See the Whole Picture

Begin with the monthly sales trends for all product categories. Comparing the lines reveals how the categories change over the same period.
[/Step]
[Step index:1]
## 2. Focus on One Category

Choose a category to examine more closely. Emphasize its sales trend while keeping the other categories visible as context.
[/Step]
[Step index:2]
## 3. Compare with the Monthly Average

Compare the selected category with the average sales across all categories in each month. The average provides a reference for identifying months when the selected category performs above or below the broader pattern.
[/Step]
[Step index:3]
## 4. Find Months Above a Threshold

Choose a sales threshold and identify the selected category’s months that exceed it. Changing the category or threshold should immediately update the highlighted observations.
[/Step]
[Pinned]
[Select value:category options:`["Books", "Games", "Music"]` /]
[Range value:threshold min:0 max:500 step:10 /]
[Display role:"stage" value:stageName /]
[Chart data:chartRows type:"line" x:"month" y:"sales" color:"category" focus:focus reference:reference highlight:highlighted /]
[/Pinned]
[/Scroller]

## Revisit the Story

Scroll back to an earlier section to revisit that perspective. Your category and threshold selections should remain available throughout the article.

tests.label: Four scroll steps with a pinned interactive chart
Reactive stage name in the pinned region
Chart behavior across categories, thresholds, and forward/reverse stages
